aliases: Sample 2 of the three Fe-C-Cr-Mn-Si alloys

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Fe-C-Cr-Mn-Si coating (Sample 2 composition) prepared by arc cladding (IDEALARC DC-1000, Lincoln Electric, America); wire with the optimized element content used as feedstock; ASTM A36 steel substrate 300 mm × 120 mm × 40 mm; current 440~600 A; voltage 30~32 V; cladding speed 24 m/h; interlayer temperature 380~410 °C; wire feed speed 76.8 m/h.

structures.overall_structure: Single main Fe-Cr-Ni solid-solution phase (bcc-type), with the (200) and (211) reflections very weak

defects.lattice_distortion: diffraction peak shifted to the right (higher 2θ) relative to the standard Fe peak due to atomic radius differences between Cr, Ni and Fe

interfaces.phase_evolution: With the Ni content increased relative to Sample 1, the main phase structure transferred from the Fe-Cr phase to the Fe-Cr-Ni phase (Sample 2).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers microhardness indenter (HVS-1000A, Laizhou Huayin Testing Instrument Co., Ltd., China); load 1 kg; holding time 20 s

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: error between predicted (490 HV) and experimental (500 HV) microhardness

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Cu Kα radiation; working voltage 40 kV; current 40 mA; 2θ range 20-100° with enlarged region 40-50°
characterization_methods.key_findings: Sample 2 main phase is Fe-Cr-Ni with diffraction peaks indexed (110), (200) and (211); (200) and (211) are very weak; the (110) peak is shifted to higher 2θ relative to the standard Fe reference, indicating lattice distortion from Cr/Ni substitution.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: HVS-1000A, Laizhou Huayin Testing Instrument Co., Ltd., China
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the Vicker's microhardness of the coatings
characterization_methods.key_findings: Sample 2 experimental microhardness = 500 HV (predicted 490 HV, 2.00% error).

computational_details.simulation_method: Support vector regression (SVR) machine-learning model combined with the modified solid solution strengthening theory
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Training/validation data from the MatWeb materials information repository
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Input features {G, δEc, DEc}; SVR hyperparameters C = 4.98, cache_size = 118.85, coef0 = 0.63, degree = 4, epsilon = 1.87 × 10⁻⁴, gamma = 3.57 × 10⁻², kernel = ploy, tol = 1.22 × 10⁻³; hyperparameters optimized by Bayesian optimization with ten-fold cross-validation
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Predicted Sample 2 microhardness = 490 HV vs experimental 500 HV (2.00% error); overall model R² = 0.89 and RMSE = 0.31 with the modified solid solution strengthening theory.

analytical_models.equation_role: Solid solution strengthening contribution ΔσSSS = Z·M·G·δEc·DEc

parameters.name: M (Taylor factor, for both FCC and BCC structures)

analytical_models.model_note: ΔσSSS = Z·M·G·δEc·DEc; introducing this term increased R² from 0.85 to 0.89 and decreased RMSE from 0.39 to 0.31.

unmapped_findings: Sample 2 nominal composition (mass%) from Table 6: C 0.53, Si 0.4, Mn 1.9, Cr 5.3, S 0.01, Ni 1.13, P 0.013, Fe 89.277, Mo 0, V 0.25, W 1.19; with δr = 0.0595 and ΔHmix = −1.213 kJ/mol.

Sample 2 satisfies the reported solid-solution formation criterion (solid solutions formed when δr < 0.066 and −11.6 < ΔHmix < 3.2 kJ/mol): its δr values fall in the reported 0.0335–0.0595 range (all < 0.066) and ΔHmix in the −1.213 to −0.451 kJ/mol range (within −11.6 to 3.2 kJ/mol).
Fig. 8 notes a labelling discrepancy: the citing text calls the peaks 100/200/211 whereas the panel labels read (110)/(200)/(211).

The FA-optimized inverse-designed composition gave the maximum designed microhardness (733.59 HV), followed by PSO (730.04 HV), GWO (708.60 HV) and SA (700.37 HV); these are design-stage ML outputs for the general Fe-C-Cr-Mn-Si system, not the measured value of Sample 2.
